nodes.label: Official UFACTORY xarm_ros2 Driver
nodes.rationale: Reuse official vendor-supported ROS 2 integration and keep vendor packages as external dependencies or documented submodules rather than casually forking them.

nodes.label: Version 1 Pick-and-Place Task
nodes.rationale: Narrow scope to one known 50 mm AprilTag-marked cube on a fixed tabletop to validate kinematics-aware evaluation, simulation-in-the-loop candidate validation, and feedback-based physical execution before expanding to clutter or unknown objects.

nodes.label: UFACTORY AG1010 Gripper
nodes.rationale: Parallel-jaw gripper; requires validating actual closed/open limits, finger motion symmetry, TCP relative to flange, actuation mapping, and MoveIt/Gazebo joint conventions against hardware rather than assuming a generic gripper model.

nodes.label: Robot State Contract
nodes.rationale: Exposes connection state, mode/error state, joint positions/velocities, motion state, gripper state, active task/trajectory IDs, and safety gate status; missing, stale, or invalid state must block new physical motion.

nodes.label: UFACTORY xArm 5
nodes.rationale: 5-DoF manipulator arm; requires verifying xArm 5-specific launch arguments, joint limits, and MoveIt model rather than assuming compatibility with other xArm models.

nodes.label: 50 mm AprilTag-Marked Cube
nodes.rationale: Known marker family, IDs, physical size, cube geometry, and marker-to-cube transforms enable deterministic pose estimation without general object recognition in Version 1.

nodes.label: Simulation Fidelity Levels 1-3
nodes.rationale: Separates Level 1 planning geometry, Level 2 motion simulation, and Level 3 contact/grasp simulation so visually animated grippers are never mistaken for validated contact physics.

nodes.label: Gazebo Digital Twin
nodes.rationale: Primary automated simulation environment for planning, collision, and sequencing validation; UFACTORY Studio is supplementary only until a programmable API is verified.

nodes.label: Version 1 Acceptance Criteria
nodes.rationale: Project is not complete merely because the robot moves; requires measured pose error, invalid candidate rejection, collision-checked planning, logged outcomes, and safety stop enforcement, without inventing numerical thresholds before baseline testing.

nodes.label: Ubuntu 24.04 and ROS 2 Jazzy Stack
nodes.rationale: Primary Linux robotics environment on ASUS ROG Zephyrus G16; WSL2 is only for secondary development and not assumed for hardware-connected ROS 2, Gazebo, and MoveIt integration.

nodes.label: Pre-Implementation Verification Backlog
nodes.rationale: Blocks autonomous physical execution until camera-to-base extrinsics, hardware limits, TCP, tool geometry, and stop behaviour are verified on actual hardware.

nodes.label: First Baseline Milestone
nodes.rationale: Requires proving xArm 5 driver, AG1010 control, RViz, MoveIt 2, and a manual Gazebo pick-and-place before adding perception-driven autonomous grasping or AI features.

nodes.label: Vertical Slice Implementation Order
nodes.rationale: Build the smallest end-to-end vertical slice first, then split/refine packages as interfaces become clear, instead of creating empty scaffolding for all packages on day one.

nodes.label: Schedule Protection Priority Policy
nodes.rationale: Protects calibration/pose, xArm/AG1010 integration, kinematic evaluation, simulation validation, and safe physical execution over dashboard or advanced AI interface work when schedule is constrained.

nodes.label: Documentation Change Control Process
nodes.rationale: Requires updating 11_DECISIONS_AND_OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, 01_PROJECT_SPECIFICATION.md, affected docs, decision history, and matching code/config whenever scope changes.

nodes.label: Version 1 Engineering Rules
nodes.rationale: Mandates vendor package reuse, clear module interfaces, deterministic safety gates over AI proposals, physical trial verification, version logging, and narrow single-cube scope.

nodes.label: Candidate Ranking Cost Function
nodes.rationale: Scores feasible candidates with normalised motion, clearance, kinematic, grasp alignment, and duration penalties; initial weights are experimental parameters tuned from recorded trials.

nodes.label: Constrained Top-Down Grasp Family
nodes.rationale: Uses deterministic top-down grasps on opposing side faces with small yaw alternatives rather than learned grasp networks or unconstrained 6-DoF generation.

nodes.label: Simulation-in-the-Loop Validation
nodes.rationale: Validates candidate trajectories in Gazebo before sending the selected candidate to the physical execution gate, while recognizing physics gaps require supervised physical trials.

nodes.label: 5-DoF Kinematic Constraints
nodes.rationale: Because xArm 5 has 5 DoF, the planner must not request arbitrary 6-DoF end-effector poses and should start with a top-down approach, aligned closing axis, limited yaw candidates, and fixed or narrowly bounded wrist orientation.

nodes.label: Hard Feasibility Constraints
nodes.rationale: Reject candidates before ranking if IK, joint limits, workspace bounds, collisions, AG1010 opening, approach/retreat paths, 5-DoF capability, or state freshness fail; weighted score must never override a hard failure.

nodes.label: Independent Grasp and Placement Verification
nodes.rationale: Combines gripper feedback, robot status, and before/after camera observation because neither a gripper closing command nor a potentially occluded camera image alone proves success.

nodes.label: System Operating Modes
nodes.rationale: Explicitly isolates MANUAL, SIMULATION, TWIN_MONITOR, and AUTONOMOUS_SUPERVISED and prohibits any mode that silently transitions from simulation to physical execution.

nodes.label: Deterministic Pre-Execution Gate
nodes.rationale: All physical movement passes through a deterministic execution manager and pre-execution gate checking robot connection, faults/e-stop, fresh state, calibration, workspace bounds, scene version, limits, and supervision; robot native safety remains primary.

nodes.label: Bounded Recovery Policy
nodes.rationale: Enforces a configurable maximum retry count (image reacquisition, replan, next-ranked candidate) and escalates to operator intervention on unpredictable displacement or faults rather than looping indefinitely.

nodes.label: AI Supervisor
nodes.rationale: Converts high-level tasks into structured requests, orchestrates perception/planning/simulation/verification, and explains results, while never sending raw joint commands or bypassing execution gates.

nodes.label: Layered ROS 2 Architecture
nodes.rationale: Each layer publishes structured data or exposes explicit services/actions so the AI supervisor coordinates high-level work without replacing deterministic perception, motion planning, robot drivers, or safety logic.

nodes.label: AI Supervisor Safety Boundary
nodes.rationale: AI supervisor may interpret tasks, coordinate tools, and explain results, but must not issue raw joint commands, bypass MoveIt validation, or override robot-native safety functions.

nodes.label: Camera-to-Robot Extrinsic Calibration
nodes.rationale: Estimates rigid transform from camera optical frame to xArm base frame using known robot-frame references; must never be inferred from a single arbitrary cube observation.

nodes.label: Camera Intrinsic Calibration
nodes.rationale: Estimates focal parameters, principal point, and distortion coefficients using a practical printed calibration target; a ChArUco board is not a Version 1 requirement.

nodes.label: Logitech C270 Camera
nodes.rationale: Fixed camera; focus and exposure should be locked where practical after setup so image characteristics remain stable across trials.

nodes.label: Fixed-Camera Calibration Policy
nodes.rationale: Camera is rigidly fixed after commissioning; saved intrinsics/extrinsics with schema version and checksum load at startup; physical camera movement invalidates calibration and requires manual recalibration.

nodes.label: Trial Logging Schema
nodes.rationale: Logs every trial including failures and aborted runs with commit/version, calibration ID, candidate scores, simulation/execution results, and operator notes for unbiased statistical reporting.

nodes.label: Primary Research Questions
nodes.rationale: Tests whether kinematic evaluation and simulation-in-the-loop improve feasibility, success, and efficiency over a fixed-grasp baseline, and measures digital twin sim-to-real predictive accuracy.

nodes.label: 5-DoF Kinematic Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Evaluates IK success, joint-limit margin, singularity conditioning, 5-DoF task-constrained manipulability, path length, duration, and collision clearance without applying an unadjusted generic 6-DoF manipulability target.

nodes.label: MoveIt 2 Motion Planning
nodes.rationale: Grasp planner requests trajectories through an explicit motion-planning interface rather than controlling MoveIt internals directly.

nodes.label: Four-Scene Synchronisation
nodes.rationale: Explicitly distinguishes Perception, Planning, Gazebo, and Physical scenes with timestamps/versions and prevents two controllers from commanding simulated joints simultaneously.

nodes.label: ai_supervisor Package (WP9)
nodes.rationale: Exposes whitelisted tools only (no joint, pose, trajectory, gate-arming, or mode-change tools).

nodes.label: Decision D3: Pluggable LLM Provider
